status_summary: NTIA issued a BEAD restructuring policy notice on 2025-06-06 for the $42.45 billion Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment program that ended the fiber preference in favor of technology neutrality (including low-earth-orbit satellite and fixed wireless), removed labor, climate and open-access requirements, rescinded earlier final proposal approvals, and required a new subgrantee round that scores lowest cost first. On 2025-12-16 GAO (decision B-337604) concluded that the notice is a rule subject to Congressional Review Act submission and stated that NTIA had not submitted it; no later submission was located. NTIA announced on 2026-08-25 that it had approved all 56 state and territory final proposals, and on 2026-09-03 it let states use a portion of roughly $21 billion in program savings for newly identified unserved locations under a supplemental deployment notice. Other NTIA items in the chapter (spectrum leasing, FirstNet review, online speech review) were not assessed here.

timeline.event: NTIA publishes the BEAD Restructuring Policy Notice ('Benefit of the Bargain'), which modifies and replaces parts of the 2022 Notice of Funding Opportunity. It removes the fiber preference and lets states choose among fiber, cable, low-earth-orbit satellite and fixed wireless (a 'Priority Broadband Project' is defined as at least 100/20 Mbps with latency of 100 ms or less that can scale to support 5G and successor technologies); sets out 'LEO Capacity Subgrants' for satellite providers; removes the NOFO's labor and workforce, climate and resilience, open-access and network-management, local coordination, non-traditional provider preference and middle-class affordability plan requirements; lets subgrantees set their own low-cost service option rates; requires at least one additional selection round with lowest total BEAD cost as the primary criterion; and rescinds earlier final proposal approvals and approval of non-deployment activities.

The notice's PDF gives states 90 days to comply and submit a Final Proposal and NTIA 90 days to review it, requires service availability within four years of a subgrant, and rescinds all Final Proposal approvals issued before the notice's publication.

GAO issues decision B-337604, at a senator's request, concluding that NTIA's 2025-06-06 BEAD Restructuring Policy Notice is a rule under the Congressional Review Act to which no exception applies, so it is subject to the Act's submission requirements; GAO notes NTIA did not submit a CRA report and does not address whether the notice is a major rule. The letter was printed in the Congressional Record on 2025-12-17 (pages S8828 to S8829).
NTIA announces approval of the last of 56 state and territory BEAD final proposals; its example for Virginia cites about 85,000 locations and about $930 million in savings.

NTIA announces that states may direct a portion of BEAD savings (about $21 billion from the reforms, per NTIA) to unserved locations identified after final proposals, under a Supplemental Deployment Policy Notice.

title: Reset NTIA broadband grant priorities toward rural deployment
uncertainties: Pass 5: the notice PDF itself was read (through a tool summary with section and page references), so the requirement changes are confirmed from the primary document; the later claims still rest on NTIA statements plus one opinion piece; no litigation or delay was found in one search, but no court docket was checked. The $21 billion savings figure is NTIA's. NTIA's national technology mix was not published in the releases read; an opinion piece in February 2026 reported large low-earth-orbit satellite allocations (about 472,600 locations for Starlink and about 415,000 for Amazon Leo), which bears on how closely the program matches the Mandate's 5G-first emphasis. Other NTIA items in the chapter (spectrum leasing, FirstNet review, online speech review) and other broadband grant programs such as digital equity grants were not assessed. Freshness check on 2026-10-21: a Federal Register search of NTIA documents from 2026-09-03 found nothing on BEAD, and the NTIA press-release index could not be fetched. The 2026-09-03 supplemental deployment notice was read through a state-hosted copy without an issue date and a Benton summary, which says other uses of the savings will come in later guidance. GAO decision B-337604 (2025-12-16) found the 2025-06-06 notice to be a rule subject to the Congressional Review Act and stated that NTIA had not submitted a CRA report; no later submission and no joint resolution of disapproval were located in web searches. The Act provides that a rule cannot take effect before submission but bars judicial review of omissions under it, so the formal legal status of the notice is unresolved; the stage rests on the final proposal approvals and on the notice having been applied in practice, which the GAO finding does not undo, while a later submission would open a disapproval window, which bears on durability. No court challenge to the notice, the final proposal approvals or the supplemental notice was located; no docket was checked.
